content: The provided text is a detailed list of drug interactions involving voriconazole and various other medications. 1. Topical roflumilast: Voriconazole can increase the systemic levels of roflumilast by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Romidepsin and voriconazole: Co-administration may lead to increased romidepsin levels and prolonged QTc interval due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 3. Rucaparib and voriconazole: Rucaparib increases voriconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4, CYP2C9/10, and CYP2C19 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 4. Ruxolitinib and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases ruxolitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib to 10 mg BID if platelet count is ≥100 x 10^9/L. Avoid use if platelet count is <100 x 10^9/L. 5. Saccharomyces boulardii: Voriconazole reduces the effects of this probiotic through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 6. Salmeterol and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases salmeterol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, which can lead to QTc prolongation. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Saxagliptin and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit saxagliptin to 5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 8. Seladelpar and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases seladelpar levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Exercise caution, especially in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers. Monitor closely. 9. Selpercatinib and voriconazole: Co-administration increases the risk of QTc prolongation and selpercatinib toxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 10. Selumetinib and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases selumetinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dose and resume the original dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 11. Sertraline and voriconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Sevoflurane and voriconazole: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 13. Sildenafil and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases sildenafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Silodosin and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases silodosin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Simvastatin and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases simvastatin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, raising the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Consider reducing the simvastatin dose if co-administered. 16. Siponimod and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases siponimod levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. 17. Sirolimus and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases sirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Sodium sulfate/potassium chloride/magnesium sulfate/polyethylene glycol and voriconazole: Both drugs decrease serum potassium levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 19. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases the levels of this combination therapy via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Solifenacin and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases solifenacin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 21. Sonidegib and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases sonidegib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 22. Sorafenib and voriconazole: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 23. Sotalol and voriconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 24. Sparsentan and voriconazole: Sparsentan decreases voriconazole levels via CYP2C9/10 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration upon resumption. 25. St. John’s Wort and voriconazole: St. John’s Wort decreases voriconazole levels by inducing metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 26. Stiripentol and voriconazole: Stiripentol increases voriconazole levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 27. Streptomycin and voriconazole: Voriconazole decreases streptomycin levels through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unclear. 28. Sufentanil and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases sufentanil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Sulfamethoxazole and voriconazole: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Sunitinib and voriconazole: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 31. Suvorexant and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases suvorexant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 32. Tacrolimus and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases tacrolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely. 33. Tadalafil and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases tadalafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Tamoxifen and voriconazole: Voriconazole inhibits tamoxifen metabolism via CYP3A4, reducing its conversion to active metabolites. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Tamsulosin and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases tamsulosin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 36. Tasimelteon and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases tasimelteon levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Tazemetostat and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases tazemetostat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 38. Tecovirimat and voriconazole: Tecovirimat affects voriconazole levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Telavancin and voriconazole: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Temsirolimus and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases temsirolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Terbinafine and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases terbinafine levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Tetrabenazine and voriconazole: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 43. Tezacaftor and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases tezacaftor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen if co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 44. Theophylline and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases theophylline levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Thioridazine and voriconazole: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 46. Tiagabine and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases tiagabine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Ticagrelor and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases ticagrelor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid use with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 48. Ticlopidine and voriconazole: Ticlopidine increases voriconazole levels via CYP2C9/10 inhibition. The clinical significance is unclear. 49. Tinidazole and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases tinidazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Tipranavir and voriconazole: Both drugs increase each other’s levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 51. Tisotumab vedotin and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases tisotumab vedotin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Tobramycin and voriconazole: Voriconazole decreases tobramycin levels through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unclear. 53. Tofacitinib and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases tofacitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg daily when co-administered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. 54. Tolterodine and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases tolterodine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Tolvaptan and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases tolvaptan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 56. Toremifene and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases toremifene levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Trabectedin and voriconazole: Voriconazole increases trabectedin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs.
